pr.title: Record the keys: MIDI takes rendered through their instrument (keyboard-instrument.md chunk 4)
pr.head: 98ca869ecd1af6dbdf8de990df6c2d9961972c74

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a MIDI instrument, and field keys <instrument> plays a SuperCollider instrument from it live. Until this pull request nothing you played could be kept. field record already records audio takes against a song: it arms field-audiod, Field's audio daemon, captures the take into a transaction directory under .field/recording/, and then lands it. Landing moves the bytes into the song, pins them in the song's ledger, and adds a row to audio/<track>/takes.yaml with the new take marked chosen.

This pull request records MIDI the same way, and it is the last chunk of the keyboard-instrument plan. A track's record: entry that names an instrument: records MIDI instead of audio. The take lands as a small text file of notes, audio/<track>/<take>.notes.yaml, and the build renders the chosen take through the instrument, placed where you played it. A take reaches the song in four steps:

1. Arm. field record sees the instrument and asks the daemon to arm for MIDI. The daemon opens every MIDI source on the machine and no audio input, so it never asks for the microphone.
  2. Capture. The daemon stamps each message on the audio callback's sample clock, so a MIDI take lines up with the song exactly as an audio take does, and appends it to take.midi.ndjson.
  3. Land. On stop, field record pairs each note-on with its note-off into the notes file, pins the file in the ledger, and writes its takes.yaml row. That row carries sources, the MIDI inputs it heard, where an audio row carries device and input.
  4. Render. The build mints a voice-render node for the chosen take. It runs sc/voice-render.scd, which plays the instrument's voice from the notes with sc/voicer.scd. The live voice host now uses the same voicer, so a take renders the way it sounded while you played.

The plan settles its three open questions about this chunk in a new §12: the take is a text list of notes, the entry is record: with an instrument, and Field's own script builds the score. §13 records the chunk as built. The criteria that need a real speaker and ears are still owed, so the plan stays in-progress.

The first review, at 8a11f14, found eight problems. The most serious was that field keys went silent after the output device changed sample rate, because the voicer's clear entry was shadowed by a built-in SuperCollider method. Five later commits fix all eight and take most of that review's smaller suggestions. The second review, at 98ca869, is clean, and the notes below say what each fix does and how it was checked.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Take. One recorded performance on a track. Audio takes are WAV files; MIDI takes are notes files.
  • Transaction. The directory .field/recording/<take>/ where the daemon writes a take in progress: its data file, manifest.json, and journal.json.
  • Landing. Turning a finished transaction into part of the song: the file, its ledger pin, and its takes.yaml row.
  • Ledger. The song's assets.yaml, which pins each committed file by its SHA-256.
  • Record entry. A - record: item in a track's inputs. It plays the chosen take where it was recorded.
  • Voice mode. An instrument program run with FIELD_MODE=voice returns a SynthDef with freq, amp, gate, and out instead of rendering.
  • Voicer. sc/voicer.scd: the rules that turn MIDI into voices, such as one voice per note, the sustain pedal, All Notes Off, and pitch bend.
  • Device samples and bed samples. The daemon's clock counts samples at the output device's rate. The bed, the song a take records against, counts at the song's rate. When the two differ, the daemon resamples the song on its way out, which the code calls converted delivery.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• First review, 8a11f14: changes requested, with one P1 and seven P2 threads. The P1 was the live voice host going silent after a rate change. The P2s were a zero-length note ringing to the end of a render, a MIDI punch-out across rates, crash buffering, the instrument path check, render variables in voice mode, a CI comment, and the plan's MIDI export.
  • Fixes: five commits fixed all eight findings, and the author resolved each thread with a reply naming its fix. They also took twelve of the fifteen suggestions.
  • Second review, 98ca869: clean, with all eight threads verified fixed. The voicer, zero-length-note, and crash reproductions were rerun at this head. Three suggestions still apply: field-level messages for a broken audio takes row, refusing --console-preset and --monitoring on a MIDI take, and an until test that sends a message the filter must drop.

groups.title: A notes file, a MIDI takes row, and the protocol that carries them
groups.kicker: The data shapes every other group reads and writes
intro: Three shapes are new, and every later group reads or writes them. The notes file is what a MIDI take becomes in the song. The MIDI takes row in takes.yaml says where the take was played. The daemon's protocol gains a MIDI arm, MIDI status fields, and a MIDI take manifest.

Field of the notes fileMeaning
sample_rateThe output device's rate during the take. Every time in the file counts in it.
lengthThe take's length in samples, from its start to the stop.
notesOne row per note: at, length, note, velocity, and channel when it is not 1.
controls, bendsController changes and pitch bends, each with its at.

notesFromMessages pairs captured messages into notes. A velocity-0 note-on counts as a note-off, a second note-on for a sounding note ends the first, and a note still held at the stop lasts to the end. renderEvents turns the notes back into on, off, controller, and bend events in seconds for the renderer. At one instant it orders offs first, then controllers and bends, then ons.

files.note: The notes file schema, its only writer, the pairing of messages into notes, and the ordered events the renderer plays.

checks.text: A note whose on and off share a sample releases. renderEvents ranks a zero-length note's off with the ons, so the off sorts directly after its own on rather than before every on at that instant. A same-instant retrigger still ends the first voice before the second starts. Checked by the new case in notes.test.ts, and by a review reproduction through real sclang whose render is silent after the note.

A blanket minimum length of one sample would not have been a safe fix. Two note-ons for the same note at one instant would then release the second note's voice one sample later. That is why the fix sits in the render order.

files.note: Pairing, the file text, and the render order, including a pad's on and off at one sample beside another note's on.
The record entry gains an optional instrument. A takes row is either the audio shape or the MIDI shape, and isMidiTakeRow tells them apart by sources.

checks.text: Both row shapes are strict, so a broken audio row now fails both branches. field check then reports Invalid input at takes.0 rather than naming the missing field. The review lists this as a suggestion.

files.note: The MIDI arm response, the MIDI take manifest, one take.midi.ndjson line, and anyTakeSchema, which tries the MIDI manifest first. An audio manifest has no kind.

groups.title: The daemon captures MIDI on the audio clock
groups.kicker: field-audiod arms for MIDI, stamps each message in the audio callback, and writes a transaction
intro: field-audiod is the C++ daemon, built on JUCE, that owns the audio device. Arming for MIDI opens every MIDI input the system lists at that moment. A message then travels through three threads:

1. JUCE's MIDI thread reads the clock when the message arrives and pushes the bytes and that time into a lock-free queue. It drops system messages such as clock and SysEx.
  2. The audio callback drains the queue at the start of each block. It stamps each message as the block's take position plus the time between the block's start and the arrival, in device samples, never earlier than the previous message.
  3. A writer thread appends the stamped messages to take.midi.ndjson every 20 ms and syncs the file and the journal once a second.

capture.cpp moves what every recording transaction shares into a Transaction base class: the directory, the manifest, the journal, the writer thread, and the list and recover commands. Capture adds the WAV file and MidiCapture adds the NDJSON file. A take with until ends at the first block that begins at or past it, and stop waits for one more block so late messages are stamped.

files.note: Arming for MIDI, the arrival queue, stamping in recordMidiBlock, the until check, and the two blocks stopRecording waits for.

checks.text: until ends on time when the song's rate is not the device's. recordMidiBlock converts the span from the bed's samples to the device's with take.timelineRate(), which is the live session's rate or the loaded file's. The daemon test's 24 kHz bed on the 48 kHz null output ends at 24000 frames. It passed in review against a build of this head.

A stop waits two callback epochs before it detaches the MIDI take. The epoch advances before a block drains MIDI, and the callback runs one block at a time, so the block that drains the last messages has finished before the detach. Checked by reading the callback order.
maybeMatchDeviceRate moves the device to a song's rate when the song loads. It holds the device still during a take and converts delivery instead, which is when the two clocks differ.

files.note: The MIDI arrival ring, the state recordMidiBlock keeps between blocks, and the opened inputs.
The Transaction base, the MIDI writer, and list and recover for both kinds of take.

checks.text: A crash keeps every whole line written. MidiCapture::drain flushes to the kernel after each 20 ms tick, not only at the once-a-second sync. A review reproduction killed the daemon 200 ms after a note-on, and the line was on disk. The daemon test now requires the note-on in the file within 500 ms.
recover for a MIDI transaction counts whole lines, truncates a partial last one, and sets frames to the larger of the journal's count and one past the last at.

files.note: The class split: Transaction, Capture, and MidiCapture, with the threading rules. timelineRate() exposes the bed's rate for the until conversion.
Routes arm with kind: "midi" and advertises record-midi.
The startup log names a recoverable MIDI take by its message count, where an audio take shows frames.

The daemon against a source published by field-audiod --keys: capture, until on a bed at the device's rate and at half of it, a crash and recovery, and field record end to end. The note it sends comes from the run's pid, so two runs on one machine stay apart.

groups.title: field record arms by the entry, and lands either kind of take
groups.kicker: Choosing the kind, refusing audio-only flags, landing a notes file, and checking the entry
intro: recordTake reads the track's record entry before it connects. With an instrument, it refuses --input, --device, and --loop, then arms for MIDI and shows an event count where an audio take shows a level meter.

land.ts now splits landing in three. beginLanding runs the checks every take needs and computes its placement. A per-kind step writes the file: landTake copies the WAV, and landMidiTake pairs the lines into a notes file. finishLanding pins the file, writes the takes.yaml row, and removes the transaction. A MIDI take's latency is the output latency alone, because you press a key in time with what you hear.
field check gains two errors: an entry whose instrument has no program, and a take of the other kind from the one its entry records.

files.note: Arming by the entry's kind, the refusal of audio-only flags, the event count, and describeTake for MIDI transactions.
beginLanding and finishLanding, which both kinds share; placeFile and sharedRow, which write the file and the row's common fields; then landMidiTake and landAnyTake.

checks.text: Placement matches the audio path. started_at_samples converts from the bed's rate to the track's, and latency converts from device samples to track samples. The helpers write the same paths and row fields the two paths wrote before. The MIDI cases in land.test.ts passed in review.

groups.title: The build renders the chosen take through its instrument
groups.kicker: A voice-render node, Field's renderer script, and the voicer it shares with the live host
intro: In the build graph, an audio record entry is replaced by a window over its chosen take's WAV. For an entry with an instrument whose chosen take is a notes file, buildGraph mints a generator node named like the record node, //songs/<song>/gen:<name>. withTakes then places that node's output where the take started, less its latency.

The node's generator, voice-render, writes renderEvents to a JSON file and runs sc/voice-render.scd with runScProgram, the same runner the supercollider: generator uses. The script loads the instrument in voice mode, drives it with the voicer to build a score, and renders in SuperCollider's non-realtime mode: stereo, at the track's rate, for the take's length plus a 4-second release tail.
sc/voicer.scd is the voicing that used to live inside sc/voice-host.scd, the live host, moved to its own file so the host and the render share it.

checks.text: The cache key covers the rule version, the notes file's hash, the instrument's content hash, the hashes of both scripts, the spec, and the track's rate. Choosing another take changes the key, and choosing back is a cache hit. Checked in actionKey in src/graph/build.ts and by voice-render.test.ts, which passed in review.

files.note: Mints the voice-render node for a chosen MIDI take, and places its output in withTakes.
The generator: its inputs, its path check, its render, and the fixed 4-second tail. Its version is 2, so renders cached before the zero-length fix are redone.

checks.text: This validate is what field check calls for a record entry with an instrument. It adds the normalized-form check the supercollider: rule makes.

files.note: The node's inputs, caching, and the render's placement at its start less the output latency. Through real sclang: a render that is the same bytes from a cold cache, and one through an instrument that throws if a render variable is set. The sclang cases skip on CI.
Registers voice-render.
Adds VoiceRenderSpec to the generator spec union.
instrumentProgram and scScript move here to be shared. runScProgram takes extra environment and allows sclang 64 MiB of output, because scsynth prints a line per score bundle in NRT.
Loads the instrument in voice mode, plays the events through the voicer into a score, and renders it.

checks.text: Voice mode looks the same in a render as live. The script reads the render variables, then unsets them before it loads the instrument, which keeps the contract in docs/build-graph.md and docs/keys.md. Checked by the real-sclang case in voice-render.test.ts.

files.note: The voicing rules, as a function of the callbacks that start, retune, and release a voice, plus an optional one told as voices start and end. It returns an Event with noteOn, noteOff, cc, bend, and forgetVoices. No entry may share a name with a method Event already has.
The live host now routes every MIDI message through the voicer.

checks.text: The live host keeps playing after a rate change. restart calls voicer.forgetVoices, a name no class in Event's chain defines. The earlier name, clear, ran Set.clear and emptied the voicer. A review reproduction in sclang found none of the voicer's entry names to be a real method, and a note played after the reset. src/keys/voicer.test.ts covers this.

Apart from the reset, the host's behavior is unchanged. The MIDIdef argument orders are right, and the voicer acts only on CC 64 and CC 123, as the base host did. Checked by reading both versions side by side.

files.note: The voicer through real sclang: a note plays after forgetVoices, the reset the host calls on restart. It skips where sclangCommand() finds no sclang.
Uses the shared instrumentProgram and scScript.
